## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

# Personal CRM

A text-based personal CRM built from email archives. Contact information is stored as markdown files with YAML frontmatter, organized by relationship type.

## Project Structure

```
client/              ~287 markdown files, one per client
colleagues/          ~8 markdown files, professional colleagues
friends/             ~20 markdown files, personal friends
mbox/                Gmail mbox exports (gitignored)
src/                 TypeScript scripts for data extraction
correspondents-filtered.csv  Curated list of 280 client emails/names
```

## Contact File Format

All contacts (clients, colleagues, friends) use the same markdown format with YAML frontmatter. Files live in the appropriate category folder (`client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/`).

### Client files (generated from Heather's mbox + Mark's Gmail)

```markdown
---
last_name: Harris
first_name: Joshua
email: "josh@clearandloud.com"
last_updated: 2026-02-14
---

## Notes

Prefers async updates over calls. Mentioned wanting to revisit pricing in Q3.

## Mark's Email History

### 2026-01-15
- **Subject:** Re: Sprint Review Follow-up
  - Direction: To client
  - Summary: Mark followed up on the sprint review action items.
  - Thread: 1856015111163477742

## Email History

### 2026-01-15
- **Subject:** Re: Sprint Review Follow-up
  - Direction: From client
  - Thread: 1856015111163477742
  - Message-ID: <CAB1234@mail.gmail.com>
```

### Colleague/Friend files (from Mark's Gmail only)

```markdown
---
last_name: DeVilla
first_name: Joey
email: "joey@globalnerdy.com"
last_updated: 2026-02-15
---

## Mark's Email History

### 2025-03-10
- **Subject:** Re: Catching up
  - Direction: From friend
  - Summary: Joey suggested meeting for coffee next week.
  - Thread: 18a4f2c3d5e6f7a8
```

### Format rules

- Entries sorted **newest to oldest**, grouped by date
- `last_updated` in frontmatter tracks when the file was last *meaningfully changed* (a new entry added, or a name backfilled). A `gmail-sync` run that finds nothing new leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged. The per-contact "last searched" cursor is deliberately **not** in the frontmatter — it lives in the gitignored `.gmail-sync-state.json` sidecar so a no-op sync produces no git diff (see `src/sync-state.ts`)
- **Direction** values: "To client/colleague/friend", "From client/colleague/friend", or "CC'd"
- **"## Notes"** section, when present, sits above "## Mark's Email History" and is authored by Mark, not generated from email data. Claude must treat it as read-only: never generate, edit, delete, or rewrite this section — leave it exactly as found. If a file has no "## Notes" section, don't add one.
- **"## Email History"** section (Heather's mbox data) exists only in `client/` files; uses Thread ID (decimal, Gmail's `X-GM-THRID`) and Message-ID (RFC 2822)
- **"## Mark's Email History"** section uses Thread ID (hex, from Gmail API) and a one-sentence Summary
- Filenames are slugified as `lastname-firstname.md`. Contacts with no known name use the email local part. Duplicate names get the email domain appended

A text-based personal CRM built from email archives. Contact information is stored as markdown files with YAML frontmatter, organized by relationship type.

client/              ~287 markdown files, one per client
colleagues/          ~8 markdown files, professional colleagues
friends/             ~20 markdown files, personal friends
mbox/                Gmail mbox exports (gitignored)

## Data Sources

### Heather's mbox (client/ files, "## Email History" section)

Client files were originally generated from an mbox export of Heather Uhl's email (former operations manager). The mbox contains emails from her accounts:
- heather.uhl@agilepainrelief.com
- heather.uhl@felicisholdings.com
- heather.uhl@smart-life-choices.com
- heatheruhl@gmail.com

### Mark's Gmail (all files, "## Mark's Email History" section)

Mark Levison's Gmail (mark@felicisholdings.com) is accessed directly via the Gmail API, using `npm run gmail-sync` (see Scripts below). Mark's email data is added to the "## Mark's Email History" section of contact files across all categories.

**Gmail access rule (mandatory):** Claude must **never** access Gmail directly — no Gmail MCP tools (e.g. `mcp__*__search_threads`, `get_thread`, `list_labels`, `create_draft`, `label_thread`), no Gmail API calls, no reading Mark's mailbox by any other means. ## Gmail Labels for Category Routing

Mark's Gmail uses labels to classify contacts into CRM categories:

| Gmail Label | CRM Folder | Description |
|-------------|------------|-------------|
| `consulting-apr-clients` | `client/` | APR consulting clients |
| `personal-friends` | `friends/` | Personal friends |

**How labels drive file creation:**
- When an email exchange involving a contact is found, check if the contact's email or thread has one of these Gmail labels applied.
- If the contact is labeled `consulting-apr-clients`, create or update their file in `client/`.
- If the contact is labeled `personal-friends`, create or update their file in `friends/`.
- If a contact already has a file in any category, update it in place regardless of labels.
- Contacts with no label match and no existing file should be flagged for Mark to classify manually.

`mbox/`, `src/`, and the `npm run` scripts are all accessible to Claude:

All scripts use TypeScript via `tsx`. Install dependencies with `npm install`.

| Command | Script | Purpose |

- Scripts handle RFC 2047 encoded headers (Base64/Q-encoding), multiline header continuation, and comma-safe address parsing.
- Client filenames are slugified as `lastname-firstname.md`. Clients with no known name use the email local part. Duplicate names get the email domain appended.

# Personal CRM

A text-based personal CRM built from email archives. Contact information is stored as markdown files with YAML frontmatter, organized by relationship type.

## Project Structure

```
client/              ~287 markdown files, one per client
colleagues/          ~8 markdown files, professional colleagues
friends/             ~20 markdown files, personal friends
mbox/                Gmail mbox exports (gitignored, no longer read by any script)
src/                 TypeScript scripts — contact creation and Gmail sync
```

## Contact File Format

All contacts (clients, colleagues, friends) use the same markdown format with YAML frontmatter. Files live in the appropriate category folder (`client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/`).

### Client files (generated from Heather's mbox + Mark's Gmail)

```markdown
---
last_name: Harris
first_name: Joshua
email: "josh@clearandloud.com"
last_updated: 2026-02-14
---

## Notes

Prefers async updates over calls. Mentioned wanting to revisit pricing in Q3.

## Mark's Email History

### 2026-01-15
- **Subject:** Re: Sprint Review Follow-up
  - Direction: To client
  - Summary: Mark followed up on the sprint review action items.
  - Thread: 1856015111163477742

## Email History

### 2026-01-15
- **Subject:** Re: Sprint Review Follow-up
  - Direction: From client
  - Thread: 1856015111163477742
  - Message-ID: <CAB1234@mail.gmail.com>
```

### Colleague/Friend files (from Mark's Gmail only)

```markdown
---
last_name: DeVilla
first_name: Joey
email: "joey@globalnerdy.com"
last_updated: 2026-02-15
---

## Mark's Email History

### 2025-03-10
- **Subject:** Re: Catching up
  - Direction: From friend
  - Summary: Joey suggested meeting for coffee next week.
  - Thread: 18a4f2c3d5e6f7a8
```

### Format rules

- Entries sorted **newest to oldest**, grouped by date
- `last_updated` in frontmatter tracks when the file was last *meaningfully changed* (a new entry added, or a name backfilled). A `gmail-sync` run that finds nothing new leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged. The per-contact "last searched" cursor is deliberately **not** in the frontmatter — it lives in the gitignored `.gmail-sync-state.json` sidecar so a no-op sync produces no git diff (see `src/sync-state.ts`)
- **Direction** values: "To client/colleague/friend", "From client/colleague/friend", or "CC'd"
- **"## Notes"** section, when present, sits above "## Mark's Email History" and is authored by Mark, not generated from email data. Claude must treat it as read-only: never generate, edit, delete, or rewrite this section — leave it exactly as found. If a file has no "## Notes" section, don't add one.
- **"## Email History"** section (Heather's mbox data) exists only in `client/` files; uses Thread ID (decimal, Gmail's `X-GM-THRID`) and Message-ID (RFC 2822)
- **"## Mark's Email History"** section uses Thread ID (hex, from Gmail API) and a one-sentence Summary
- Filenames are slugified as `lastname-firstname.md`. Contacts with no known name use the email local part. Duplicate names get the email domain appended
- The frontmatter key is always `email:` — for one address use an inline string (`email: "x@y.com"`); for several, a block list (`email:` then `  - "..."` lines). The reader (`parseFrontmatterEmails` in `src/frontmatter.ts`) is tolerant: it also accepts the legacy plural `emails:` key and an inline array, so old files keep working, but new files should use `email:` for every shape

## Data Sources

### Heather's mbox (client/ files, "## Email History" section)

Client files were originally generated from an mbox export of Heather Uhl's email (former operations manager). The mbox contains emails from her accounts:
- heather.uhl@agilepainrelief.com
- heather.uhl@felicisholdings.com
- heather.uhl@smart-life-choices.com
- heatheruhl@gmail.com

### Mark's Gmail (all files, "## Mark's Email History" section)

Mark Levison's Gmail (mark@felicisholdings.com) is accessed directly via the Gmail API, using `npm run gmail-sync` (see Scripts below). Mark's email data is added to the "## Mark's Email History" section of contact files across all categories.

**Gmail access rule (mandatory):** Claude must **never** access Gmail directly — no Gmail MCP tools (e.g. `mcp__*__search_threads`, `get_thread`, `list_labels`, `create_draft`, `label_thread`), no Gmail API calls, no reading Mark's mailbox by any other means. All Gmail interaction happens **only** through the human running `npm run gmail-sync` (and `npm run gmail-login`) locally. When a task needs Gmail data, ask Mark to run `gmail-sync` and share the output, or work from the mbox / existing markdown files instead. This is enforced by `deny` rules in `.claude/settings.json`.

## Gmail Labels for Category Routing

Mark's Gmail uses labels to classify contacts into CRM categories:

| Gmail Label | CRM Folder | Description |
|-------------|------------|-------------|
| `consulting-apr-clients` | `client/` | APR consulting clients |
| `personal-friends` | `friends/` | Personal friends |

**How labels drive file creation:**
- When an email exchange involving a contact is found, check if the contact's email or thread has one of these Gmail labels applied.
- If the contact is labeled `consulting-apr-clients`, create or update their file in `client/`.
- If the contact is labeled `personal-friends`, create or update their file in `friends/`.
- If a contact already has a file in any category, update it in place regardless of labels.
- Contacts with no label match and no existing file should be flagged for Mark to classify manually.
- Note: `gmail-sync` only updates contacts that already have a file (it discovers files under `client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/` rather than searching Gmail for unknown contacts) — creating a file for a brand-new contact is still a manual step.

## Full Repo Access

`mbox/`, `src/`, and the `npm run` scripts are all accessible to Claude:

- **`mbox/`** — Contains raw email exports with private correspondence. No script reads it any more, but Claude may still grep it directly (e.g., to look up a contact's old threads) — treat the contents as sensitive and don't copy more into markdown files than the task at hand needs.
- **`src/`** — TypeScript scripts for contact creation and Gmail sync. Claude may read, write, and modify these scripts.
- **`npm run` commands** — Claude may run the scripts listed under Scripts below, except `gmail-login`/`gmail-sync` (see the Gmail access rule).

Claude's primary role is still working with the **markdown files in `client/`**, `colleagues/`, and `friends/`, but Claude can now go directly to the mbox and scripts when a task calls for it instead of asking the user to do so.

## Scripts

All scripts use TypeScript via `tsx`. Install dependencies with `npm install`.

| Command | Script | Purpose |
|---------|--------|---------|
| `npm run create-contact -- --name "First Last" --email a@b.com [--email ...] --category client\|colleague\|friend` | `src/create-contact.ts` | Create a new contact markdown file in the given category folder. |
| `npm run gmail-login` | `src/gmail-login.ts` | One-time OAuth login for Mark's Gmail API access; run before the first `gmail-sync`. |
| `npm run gmail-sync -- [contact.md ...]` | `src/gmail-sync.ts` | Incrementally update contact files from Mark's Gmail via the Gmail API. With no file args, scans every existing file in `client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/`. Searches each contact's address(es), dedups against entries already in the file, optionally summarizes new messages with a local Ollama model, and merges (never overwrites) via `mergeContact` in `src/merge.ts`. Each contact's search cursor is read from and written to `.gmail-sync-state.json` (gitignored, `src/sync-state.ts`) — advancing it never touches the contact file, so no-op runs stay out of git. `--dry-run` previews without writing; `--no-summarize` skips the Summary line. This is the live path for updating "## Mark's Email History" — replaces the old Claude Cowork/Gmail-connector workflow. |
| `npx tsx src/migrate-last-searched.ts` | `src/migrate-last-searched.ts` | **Historic** — one-time migration that moved the old per-file `last_searched:` frontmatter cursor into `.gmail-sync-state.json` and stripped the dead line. Idempotent (`--dry-run` to preview). Already applied; safe to re-run but does nothing now. |

The mbox-scraping scripts (`extract`, `filter`, `senders`, `clients`, `search-mbox`) have been dropped from `package.json`. They were a one-time bootstrap that originally generated `client/` from Heather's mbox plus `correspondents-filtered.csv`; ongoing updates go through `gmail-sync`, which merges instead of overwriting. The `src/` files remain on disk for reference but are no longer wired up as npm scripts.

## Technical Notes

- The mbox file is ~8 GB and gitignored. It lives in `mbox/`. Nothing in the live pipeline reads it any more — grep it directly if you need to look something up.
- Scripts handle RFC 2047 encoded headers (Base64/Q-encoding), multiline header continuation, and comma-safe address parsing.
- Client filenames are slugified as `lastname-firstname.md`. Clients with no known name use the email local part. Duplicate names get the email domain appended.

# CLAUDE.md Improver

Audit, evaluate, and improve CLAUDE.md files across a codebase to ensure Claude Code has optimal project context.

**This skill can write to CLAUDE.md files.** After presenting a quality report and getting user approval, it updates CLAUDE.md files with targeted improvements.

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Discovery

Find all CLAUDE.md files in the repository:

```bash
find . -name "CLAUDE.md" -o -name ".claude.md" -o -name ".claude.local.md" 2>/dev/null | head -50
```

**File Types & Locations:**

| Type | Location | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| Project root | `./CLAUDE.md` | Primary project context (checked into git, shared with team) |
| Local overrides | `./.claude.local.md` | Personal/local settings (gitignored, not shared) |
| Global defaults | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | User-wide defaults across all projects |
| Package-specific | `./packages/*/CLAUDE.md` | Module-level context in monorepos |
| Subdirectory | Any nested location | Feature/domain-specific context |

**Note:** Claude auto-discovers CLAUDE.md files in parent directories, making monorepo setups work automatically.

### Phase 2: Quality Assessment

For each CLAUDE.md file, evaluate against quality criteria. See [references/quality-criteria.md](references/quality-criteria.md) for detailed rubrics.

**Quick Assessment Checklist:**

| Criterion | Weight | Check |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Commands/workflows documented | High | Are build/test/deploy commands present? |
| Architecture clarity | High | Can Claude understand the codebase structure? |
| Non-obvious patterns | Medium | Are gotchas and quirks documented? |
| Conciseness | Medium | No verbose explanations or obvious info? |
| Currency | High | Does it reflect current codebase state? |
| Actionability | High | Are instructions executable, not vague? |

**Quality Scores:**
- **A (90-100)**: Comprehensive, current, actionable
- **B (70-89)**: Good coverage, minor gaps
- **C (50-69)**: Basic info, missing key sections
- **D (30-49)**: Sparse or outdated
- **F (0-29)**: Missing or severely outdated

### Phase 3: Quality Report Output

**ALWAYS output the quality report BEFORE making any updates.**

Format:

```
## CLAUDE.md Quality Report

### Summary
- Files found: X
- Average score: X/100
- Files needing update: X

### File-by-File Assessment

#### 1. ./CLAUDE.md (Project Root)
**Score: XX/100 (Grade: X)**

| Criterion | Score | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Commands/workflows | X/20 | ... |
| Architecture clarity | X/20 | ... |
| Non-obvious patterns | X/15 | ... |
| Conciseness | X/15 | ... |
| Currency | X/15 | ... |
| Actionability | X/15 | ... |

**Issues:**
- [List specific problems]

**Recommended additions:**
- [List what should be added]

#### 2. ./packages/api/CLAUDE.md (Package-specific)
...
```

### Phase 4: Targeted Updates

After outputting the quality report, ask user for confirmation before updating.

**Update Guidelines (Critical):**

1. **Propose targeted additions only** - Focus on genuinely useful info:
   - Commands or workflows discovered during analysis
   - Gotchas or non-obvious patterns found in code
   - Package relationships that weren't clear
   - Testing approaches that work
   - Configuration quirks

2. **Keep it minimal** - Avoid:
   - Restating what's obvious from the code
   - Generic best practices already covered
   - One-off fixes unlikely to recur
   - Verbose explanations when a one-liner suffices

3. **Show diffs** - For each change, show:
   - Which CLAUDE.md file to update
   - The specific addition (as a diff or quoted block)
   - Brief explanation of why this helps future sessions

**Diff Format:**

```markdown
### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** Build command was missing, causing confusion about how to run the project.

```diff
+ ## Quick Start
+
+ ```bash
+ npm install
+ npm run dev  # Start development server on port 3000
+ ```
```
```

### Phase 5: Apply Updates

After user approval, apply changes using the Edit tool. Preserve existing content structure.

## Templates

See [references/templates.md](references/templates.md) for CLAUDE.md templates by project type.

## Common Issues to Flag

1. **Stale commands**: Build commands that no longer work
2. **Missing dependencies**: Required tools not mentioned
3. **Outdated architecture**: File structure that's changed
4. **Missing environment setup**: Required env vars or config
5. **Broken test commands**: Test scripts that have changed
6. **Undocumented gotchas**: Non-obvious patterns not captured

## User Tips to Share

When presenting recommendations, remind users:

- **`#` key shortcut**: During a Claude session, press `#` to have Claude auto-incorporate learnings into CLAUDE.md
- **Keep it concise**: CLAUDE.md should be human-readable; dense is better than verbose
- **Actionable commands**: All documented commands should be copy-paste ready
- **Use `.claude.local.md`**: For personal preferences not shared with team (add to `.gitignore`)
- **Global defaults**: Put user-wide preferences in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

**Key principles:**
- Concise and human-readable
- Actionable commands that can be copy-pasted
- Project-specific patterns, not generic advice
- Non-obvious gotchas and warnings

**Recommended sections** (use only what's relevant):
- Commands (build, test, dev, lint)
- Architecture (directory structure)
- Key Files (entry points, config)
- Code Style (project conventions)
- Environment (required vars, setup)
- Testing (commands, patterns)
- Gotchas (quirks, common mistakes)

# Personal CRM

A text-based personal CRM built from email archives. Contact information is stored as markdown files with YAML frontmatter, organized by relationship type.

## Project Structure

```
client/              one markdown file per client
colleagues/          professional colleagues
friends/             personal friends
mbox/                Gmail mbox exports (gitignored, no longer read by any script)
src/                 TypeScript scripts — contact creation and Gmail sync
```

## Contact File Format

All contacts (clients, colleagues, friends) use the same markdown format with YAML frontmatter. Files live in the appropriate category folder (`client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/`).

### Client files (generated from Heather's mbox + Mark's Gmail)

```markdown
---
last_name: Harris
first_name: Joshua
email: "josh@clearandloud.com"
last_updated: 2026-02-14
---

## Notes

Prefers async updates over calls. Mentioned wanting to revisit pricing in Q3.

## Mark's Email History

### 2026-01-15
- **Subject:** Re: Sprint Review Follow-up
  - Direction: To client
  - Summary: Mark followed up on the sprint review action items.
  - Thread: 1856015111163477742

## Email History

### 2026-01-15
- **Subject:** Re: Sprint Review Follow-up
  - Direction: From client
  - Thread: 1856015111163477742
  - Message-ID: <CAB1234@mail.gmail.com>
```

### Colleague/Friend files (from Mark's Gmail only)

```markdown
---
last_name: DeVilla
first_name: Joey
email: "joey@globalnerdy.com"
last_updated: 2026-02-15
---

## Mark's Email History

### 2025-03-10
- **Subject:** Re: Catching up
  - Direction: From friend
  - Summary: Joey suggested meeting for coffee next week.
  - Thread: 18a4f2c3d5e6f7a8
```

### Format rules

- Entries sorted **newest to oldest**, grouped by date
- `last_updated` in frontmatter tracks when the file was last *meaningfully changed* (a new entry added, or a name backfilled). A `gmail-sync` run that finds nothing new leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged. The per-contact "last searched" cursor is deliberately **not** in the frontmatter — it lives in the gitignored `.gmail-sync-state.json` sidecar so a no-op sync produces no git diff (see `src/sync-state.ts`)
- **Direction** values: "To client/colleague/friend", "From client/colleague/friend", or "CC'd"
- **"## Notes"** section, when present, sits above "## Mark's Email History" and is authored by Mark, not generated from email data. Claude must treat it as read-only: never generate, edit, delete, or rewrite this section — leave it exactly as found. If a file has no "## Notes" section, don't add one.
- **"## Email History"** section (Heather's mbox data) exists only in `client/` files; uses Thread ID (decimal, Gmail's `X-GM-THRID`) and Message-ID (RFC 2822)
- **"## Mark's Email History"** section uses Thread ID (hex, from Gmail API) and a one-sentence Summary
- Filenames are slugified as `lastname-firstname.md`. Contacts with no known name use the email local part. Duplicate names get the email domain appended
- The frontmatter key is always `email:` — for one address use an inline string (`email: "x@y.com"`); for several, a block list (`email:` then `  - "..."` lines). The reader (`parseFrontmatterEmails` in `src/frontmatter.ts`) is tolerant: it also accepts the legacy plural `emails:` key and an inline array, so old files keep working, but new files should use `email:` for every shape

## Data Sources

### Heather's mbox (client/ files, "## Email History" section)

Client files were originally generated from an mbox export of Heather Uhl's email (former operations manager). The mbox contains emails from her accounts:
- heather.uhl@agilepainrelief.com
- heather.uhl@felicisholdings.com
- heather.uhl@smart-life-choices.com
- heatheruhl@gmail.com

### Mark's Gmail (all files, "## Mark's Email History" section)

Mark Levison's Gmail (mark@felicisholdings.com) is accessed directly via the Gmail API, using `npm run gmail-sync` (see Scripts below). Mark's email data is added to the "## Mark's Email History" section of contact files across all categories.

**Gmail access rule (mandatory):** Claude must **never** access Gmail directly — no Gmail MCP tools (e.g. `mcp__*__search_threads`, `get_thread`, `list_labels`, `create_draft`, `label_thread`), no Gmail API calls, no reading Mark's mailbox by any other means. All Gmail interaction happens **only** through the human running `npm run gmail-sync` (and `npm run gmail-login`) locally. When a task needs Gmail data, ask Mark to run `gmail-sync` and share the output, or work from the mbox / existing markdown files instead. This is enforced by `deny` rules in `.claude/settings.json`.

## Gmail Labels for Category Routing

Mark's Gmail uses labels to classify contacts into CRM categories:

| Gmail Label | CRM Folder | Description |
|-------------|------------|-------------|
| `consulting-apr-clients` | `client/` | APR consulting clients |
| `personal-friends` | `friends/` | Personal friends |

**How labels drive file creation:**
- When an email exchange involving a contact is found, check if the contact's email or thread has one of these Gmail labels applied.
- If the contact is labeled `consulting-apr-clients`, create or update their file in `client/`.
- If the contact is labeled `personal-friends`, create or update their file in `friends/`.
- If a contact already has a file in any category, update it in place regardless of labels.
- Contacts with no label match and no existing file should be flagged for Mark to classify manually.
- Note: `gmail-sync` only updates contacts that already have a file (it discovers files under `client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/` rather than searching Gmail for unknown contacts) — creating a file for a brand-new contact is still a manual step.

## Full Repo Access

`mbox/`, `src/`, and the `npm run` scripts are all accessible to Claude:

- **`mbox/`** — Contains raw email exports with private correspondence. No script reads it any more, but Claude may still grep it directly (e.g., to look up a contact's old threads) — treat the contents as sensitive and don't copy more into markdown files than the task at hand needs.
- **`src/`** — TypeScript scripts for contact creation and Gmail sync. Claude may read, write, and modify these scripts.
- **`npm run` commands** — Claude may run the scripts listed under Scripts below, except `gmail-login`/`gmail-sync` (see the Gmail access rule).

Claude's primary role is still working with the **markdown files in `client/`**, `colleagues/`, and `friends/`, but Claude can now go directly to the mbox and scripts when a task calls for it instead of asking the user to do so.

All scripts use TypeScript via `tsx`. Install dependencies with `npm install`.

|---------|--------|---------|
| `npm run create-contact -- --name "First Last" --email a@b.com [--email ...] --category client\|colleague\|friend` | `src/create-contact.ts` | Create a new contact markdown file in the given category folder. |
| `npm run gmail-login` | `src/gmail-login.ts` | One-time OAuth login for Mark's Gmail API access; run before the first `gmail-sync`. |
| `npm run gmail-sync -- [contact.md ...]` | `src/gmail-sync.ts` | Incrementally update contact files from Mark's Gmail via the Gmail API. With no file args, scans every existing file in `client/`, `colleagues/`, `friends/`. Searches each contact's address(es), dedups against entries already in the file, optionally summarizes new messages with a local Ollama model, and merges (never overwrites) via `mergeContact` in `src/merge.ts`. Idempotent (`--dry-run` to preview). Already applied; safe to re-run but does nothing now. |

The mbox-scraping scripts (`extract`, `filter`, `senders`, `clients`, `search-mbox`) and their `correspondents*.csv` artifacts have been **deleted**. They were a one-time bootstrap that generated `client/` from Heather's mbox; ongoing updates go through `gmail-sync`, which merges instead of overwriting. Nothing in the repo reads the mbox any more. If you ever need to see how `client/` was originally built, recover the scripts from git history (they were removed on the commit that also trimmed this section).
